les: Die ster wat ons bedags sien
kaps_punt: Ons naaste ster - die Son is 'n ster; die Son bestaan uit warm gas en gee hitte en lig af; die Son is baie groot (baie groter as die Aarde); die Son is baie ver weg, maar dit is die naaste ster aan die Aarde; die Son verskaf hitte en lig na die Aarde en lewende dinge

items.bewering: Die meeste van daardie klein liggies is sterre, en hulle staan baie ver in die buiteruim.
items.bron: Proxima Centauri, the nearest star after the Sun, is about 4.24 light-years (~40 trillion km) away (EarthSky, HyperPhysics GSU). Most naked-eye night lights are stars, and a few are planets, so 'die meeste' is accurate.

items.bewering: Bedags is die lug so lig dat jy nie een van hulle kan sien nie.
items.bron: Correct if 'hulle' means the stars, which is the nearest plural noun. Even bright stars (magnitude 0 to 1) are far too faint for ordinary daylight. Note: Venus, one of the 'klein liggies' but a planet, can be seen by day with the naked eye under good conditions (Fourmilab, Orwell Astronomical Society). The sentence is still true on the natural reading, and no fix is needed.

items.bewering: Tog is daar een ster wat jy elke helder dag kan sien. Die helderste ding bedags in die lug is self 'n ster, en ons noem hom die Son.
items.bron: The Sun is a star and the brightest object in the daytime sky (NASA SVS; astronomie.nl: 'De dichtstbijzijnde ster voor de Aarde is natuurlijk de Zon'). Superlative 'helderste' holds.

items.bewering: Die Son is 'n groot bal wat heeltemal uit baie warm gas bestaan.
items.bron: NASA SVS (Parker 'touches the Sun' script): the Sun is 'a giant ball of hot plasma held together by its own gravity'. Plasma is ionised gas, so 'warm gas' is an acceptable Grade 4 simplification and matches the CAPS wording (Aalto University; astronomie.nl 'bollen van gloeiend heet gas').

items.bewering: Daar is dus nêrens op die Son 'n plek waar jy sou kon staan nie.
items.bron: NASA SVS: the Sun 'lacks a solid surface like Earth's'; UCAR HAO 'Does the Sun have a surface?': the photosphere is opaque gas, not a solid surface.

items.bewering: Die Son se lig kan 'n mens se oë beskadig, en daardie skade kan blywend wees.
items.bron: Moorfields Eye Hospital (NHS): solar retinopathy, and permanent vision loss can occur. NBC News expert: about a quarter of solar retinopathy patients have permanent damage. 'kan blywend wees' is the right strength: not always permanent, but it can be.

items.bewering: Kyk daarom nooit reguit na die Son sonder regte beskerming vir jou oë nie. Sulke beskerming word spesiaal daarvoor gemaak, en 'n gewone sonbril bied dit nie.
items.bron: Moorfields (NHS) and Northeastern University: ordinary sunglasses, even very dark ones, do not protect against looking directly at the Sun. NASA: use purpose-made viewers meeting ISO 12312-2. 'spesiaal daarvoor gemaak' correctly rules out home-made or improvised filters.

items.bewering: Kyk ook nooit deur 'n verkyker of 'n teleskoop na die Son nie, selfs nie met die spesiale beskerming aan nie. Die verkyker of teleskoop maak die lig so sterk dat dit deur die beskerming kan brand.
items.bron: AAS updated eclipse-safety advice: do not look at the Sun through a camera lens, telescope, binoculars or any optical device while wearing eclipse glasses or a hand-held viewer, because the concentrated solar rays will burn through the filter and cause serious eye injury. The lesson matches this almost word for word. It is stricter than AAS on one point: a certified solar filter fitted to the FRONT of a telescope is safe. That strictness errs on the safe side for a Grade 4 learner, so it is not a fault.

items.bewering: Oogveiligheid as geheel (die sinne saam gelees, ook teen 'Tog is daar een ster wat jy elke helder dag kan sien'): mag 'n leerder iets onveiligs aflei?
items.bron: Read together, the sentences say: (1) the Sun can be seen every clear day, which means seeing it in the sky, not staring at it; (2) its light can damage eyes permanently; (3) never look straight at it without purpose-made protection, and sunglasses are not that; (4) never through binoculars or a telescope, even with that protection on, because the concentrated light can burn through. Nothing permits a short naked-eye glance, sunglasses, improvised filters, or optics plus glasses. The one thing permitted, looking with purpose-made protection, is what NASA and AAS endorse (ISO 12312-2). No unsafe conclusion follows. Checked against AAS, NASA and Moorfields as above.

items.bewering: Die Aarde is 'n groot ronde bal, en jy sien net 'n klein stukkie daarvan.
items.bron: Earth is an approximately spherical planet, about 12,742 km across (standard reference value; Sky at Night Magazine). A person on the ground sees only a tiny part of it.

items.bewering: Die Son is ook 'n ronde bal, en hy is baie groter as die Aarde.
items.bron: The Sun's diameter is about 109 times Earth's (Sky at Night Magazine; Universe Today).

items.bewering: Stel jou voor die Son is hol en jy kan Aardes daarin gooi. Honderdduisende Aardes sou in die Son pas.
items.bron: By volume about 1.3 million Earths fit in the Sun. As whole spheres thrown into a hollow Sun, which is the picture the analogy draws, packing allows about 960,000 (Sky at Night Magazine; Universe Today). So 'honderdduisende' is accurate for the analogy as worded, though at its upper edge. The mapping holds: whole balls leave gaps, so fewer fit than the pure volume ratio, and the lesson's figure fits that picture. A learner reasoning further does not go wrong. Optional, not required: 'amper 'n miljoen' would be just as true and convey the scale better.

items.bewering: Die Son lyk groot in ons lug, maar hy is baie ver van die Aarde af. As jy met 'n motor daarheen kon ry, sou die reis meer as honderd jaar duur.
items.blok: Ver weg, en tog die naaste ster
items.bron: Sun–Earth distance is about 149.6 million km (astronomie.nl; ~93 million miles in EarthSky). Arithmetic: driving non-stop at 120 km/h takes about 1.25 million hours, about 142 years. At 100 km/h it is about 171 years. Only above about 170 km/h would it drop below 100 years. So 'meer as honderd jaar' holds for any ordinary driving speed.

items.bewering: Die ander sterre is nog baie verder weg as die Son. Die Son is daarom die naaste ster aan die Aarde.
items.blok: Ver weg, en tog die naaste ster
items.bron: The nearest other star, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.24 light-years away, roughly 270,000 times the Earth–Sun distance (EarthSky; HyperPhysics GSU 'Stellar Neighbors of the Sun'; Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Lys van naaste sterre' places the Sun first). Superlative 'naaste' holds.

items.bewering: Dit is hoekom hy vir ons so groot en so helder lyk. Die ander sterre lyk vir ons net soos klein kolletjies in die nag.
items.blok: Ver weg, en tog die naaste ster
items.bron: astronomie.nl: other stars seen up close would look like the Sun, and they look small and faint only because they are so far away. The Sun's apparent size and brightness come from its proximity.

items.bewering: Party van hulle is eintlik groter as die Son. Daardie groter sterre lyk vir ons klein en dof omdat hulle so ver weg is.
items.blok: Ver weg, en tog die naaste ster
items.bron: NASA (science.nasa.gov, 'What is Betelgeuse?'): Betelgeuse is about 700 times the Sun's size. Mu Cephei and VY Canis Majoris are larger still. 'Party' is the correct quantifier, since many stars are smaller than the Sun. Distance is why they look small and faint (astronomie.nl).

items.bewering: Die Son se hitte en lig reis deur die buiteruim tot by die Aarde. Daardie lig verlig bedags ons hele wêreld.
items.blok: Wat die Son vir die Aarde doen
items.bron: Sunlight and infrared radiation cross near-empty space to Earth (outer space is a near-perfect vacuum: New World Encyclopedia 'Outer space'). 'ons hele wêreld' read as the daylit side is fine at Grade 4.

items.bewering: Die Son se hitte maak die grond, die lug en die see om jou warm. Sonder daardie hitte sou die Aarde 'n baie koue plek wees.
items.blok: Wat die Son vir die Aarde doen
items.bron: Solar radiation is the main energy input heating Earth's surface, oceans and atmosphere. The NOAA PMEL vent material contrasts sunlit ecosystems with the cold, dark deep sea, where no sunlight reaches. Consistent with standard Earth science.

items.bewering: 'n Groen plant gebruik die Son se lig om sy eie kos te maak.
items.blok: Lewende dinge het die Son nodig
items.bron: Photosynthesis: most life on Earth depends on photosynthesis, in which green plants use light to make food (PBS NOVA 'Life in the Abyss'; NOAA PMEL contrasts this with chemosynthesis).

items.bewering: 'n Bok vreet sulke plante, en 'n mens eet die plante en die bok. So beweeg die Son se energie van die plant tot op jou bord.
items.blok: Lewende dinge het die Son nodig
items.bron: This is a standard food chain, Sun to plant to herbivore to human, and the mapping holds (PBS NOVA: other life derives its energy directly or indirectly from the Sun). Goats graze and browse plants, and people eat both. The verbs are right too: 'vreet' for the animal, 'eet' for the person.

items.bewering: Die Son se hitte hou die Aarde ook warm genoeg vir die lewe wat ons ken. Byna alle lewende dinge het daardie hitte en lig nodig.
items.blok: Lewende dinge het die Son nodig
items.bron: PBS NOVA 'Life in the Abyss' and NOAA PMEL: almost all life depends, directly or indirectly, on the Sun. The known exception is chemosynthetic communities such as hydrothermal vents (NOAA; University of Bergen), so 'byna alle' is the correct quantifier. Read right after the energy-chain sentence, 'nodig' means needs, through the food chain. Read in isolation it could suggest every mushroom or cave animal needs light itself, but in context the claim is sound.

items.bewering: ster: 'n Baie groot bal warm gas wat sy eie lig maak.
items.bron: Read alone and in context: stars are large, self-luminous balls of hot gas (plasma) that make their own light by nuclear fusion (astronomie.nl: 'grote bollen van gloeiend heet gas die zelf licht en warmte produceren'). Even small stars (red dwarfs) are huge compared with Earth, so 'baie groot' holds. The entry does not wrongly include planets, which do not make their own light.

items.bewering: gas: Materiaal sonder eie vorm wat versprei en 'n hele houer vul.
items.bron: Read alone: Britannica Kids 'Gas': gases have neither a definite shape nor a definite volume and expand to fill their container. Purdue General Chemistry: gases expand to fill their containers. 'versprei en 'n hele houer vul' is what tells a gas apart from a liquid, which also has no shape of its own, so the entry does not define a liquid by mistake.

items.bewering: buiteruim: Die groot, amper leë ruimte buite die Aarde waar die sterre is.
items.bron: Read alone: outer space is a near-perfect vacuum beyond Earth's atmosphere, not perfectly empty (New World Encyclopedia 'Outer space'). 'amper leë' is the correct qualifier. 'waar die sterre is' is true and not exclusive.

opsomming: Elke kontroleerbare bewering, al drie begrip-inskrywings (ook elkeen alleen gelees) en die oogveiligheidsinne saam gelees is teen bronne bevestig (AAS, NASA, Moorfields/NHS, EarthSky, HyperPhysics, NOAA): die veiligheidsteks laat geen onveilige afleiding toe nie, want sonbrille en verkyker/teleskoop-met-bril word albei uitdruklik verbied, soos AAS dit stel; 'honderdduisende Aardes' is waar vir heel balle (ongeveer 960 000) maar sit aan die boonste rand, en 'amper 'n miljoen' sou die skaal beter oordra (opsioneel).
